text:
B: Hello. Can you hear me?
A: Erm, yes. Hi. I'm Kezia.
B: Joanne. I'm in Frome, in Somerset.
A: I'm in Catford. South East London.
B: I'll be honest, I liked the scripture on your wall. In the photo.
A: Oh. Thank you. Darren said that as well, actually.
B: Did he? Well. It's a good one. Do you go to church?
A: Most Sundays. With my mum. I'm in the choir. Do you go?
B: Now and then. Christmas, Easter. Erm. Sometimes I just go and sit in there on my own, if work's been bad. It's quiet. That sort of helps.
A: Yeah. I understand that. What do you do for work?
B: Senior carer. Dementia home. Twelve-hour shifts, mostly.
A: That must be really hard.
B: It can be. You get attached. And then you lose them. That's the bit nobody tells you about. What do you do?
A: I'm a teaching assistant. SEN. Two children with autism, in Year 3.
B: That's not easy either.
A: Erm, it's sort of about routine. If I keep things the same, it goes well. I make visual timetables, and we use Makaton.
B: We use pictures with some of ours as well. Cards for drink, toilet, that kind of thing. When the words go, sometimes the pictures still work.
A: Oh, really? I didn't know that. That's the same thing, kind of.
B: It is. It's just the other end of life. Same idea. Don't rush them, show them, give them time.
A: Yeah. That's exactly it. The teachers want everything quick, and they can't do quick.
B: Neither can mine. Do you enjoy it, though?
A: Yeah. I do. I'm thinking about doing HLTA, higher level, in a couple of years. I worry it's too much, though. Is that okay, sorry?
B: Of course. I'm doing a Level 4 now, through work. I worry about the same thing. Becoming all paperwork. Losing the residents.
A: I wouldn't want to lose the kids. That's the good bit.
B: Exactly. Erm. Have you got family nearby?
A: My mum and dad, in Sydenham. Sunday dinner there after church. I live on my own, though. In a flat.
B: Do you like that?
A: Erm. I'm getting used to it. It was a bit scary at first. I've got plants now. A peace lily I keep overwatering.
B: I've got a son, fourteen, and a greyhound, so it's never quiet at mine. Sometimes I'd quite like a peace lily instead.
A: Ha. Yeah. The lily doesn't talk back, at least, but my mum says I fuss over it like—
